title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows and Risk Exceptions
author: Priya Shah
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s operational guidance for security and compliance across seven topic areas: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exceptions. It is intended for service owners, SRE, platform, product, and security reviewers responsible for delivering auditable controls.

Scope

- Applies to all hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and to the control plane, customer-facing APIs, internal admin consoles, and CI/CD systems.
- Excludes third-party vendor control implementations (see vendor assessment playbook).

1) RBAC & Authentication

Goal: Provide least-privilege, auditable access controls for all systems and services.

Overview:
- Primary identity provider: corporate SSO (OIDC/SAML) with MFA required for all human users.
- Service-to-service authentication: short-lived mTLS or workload identity tokens (Vault/JWT), rotated automatically.
- Admin operations require elevated role jump (just-in-time sudo via approval workflow).

Roles and permissions (recommended baseline):
- Viewer: read-only access to dashboards, logs, and metrics. No config or run actions.
- Developer: deploy and run workloads in non-prod; read access to prod metadata; no PII access.
- Operator: manage runtime configs, scale, and incident actions; no billing or customer data export.
- Security Admin: manage RBAC policies, review audit logs, request evidence.
- Platform Admin: full control over infra; scoped to Dedicated/VPC tenants when required.

Implementation checkpoints (must be verified by security owners):
1. All roles expressed in central IAM and enforced via service gateways (authz layer).
2. No long-lived static keys for humans or services.
3. Role change processes require JIRA ticket and owner approval; changes are audited.
4. Privileged sessions are logged and recorded; screen capture for high-risk operations is enabled where feasible.

Example role policy (pseudo-JSON for policy registry):

```
{
  "role": "operator",
  "allow": ["runtime.scale","runtime.rollback","alerts.acknowledge"],
  "deny": ["billing.export","customer.data.export"]
}
```

2) Audit Logging

Goal: Ensure reliable, tamper-evident, and searchable audit trails for security-relevant actions.

Requirements:
- Audit sources: application authz events, admin console actions, CI/CD pipeline runs, vault/secret access events, network edge requests (proxy), and cloud IAM events.
- Ingestion SLA: 99.9% of audit events ingested within 2 minutes of occurrence.
- Integrity: append-only storage with write-once retention and cryptographic checksums for high-sensitivity logs.
- Access: logs accessible to Security and authorized auditors; access to raw logs requires an approved request.

Retention and storage tiers (see Data Residency section for residency constraints):
| Log type | Minimum retention | Storage class | Integrity controls |
|---|---:|---|---|
| AuthN/AuthZ events | 2 years | hot-archive | WORM + checksums |
| Admin console actions | 3 years | cold-archive | WORM + signed manifests |
| CI/CD pipeline logs | 1 year | warm | standard immutability |
| Edge request traces | 90 days | hot | sampled hashing |

Alerting and monitoring:
- Missing log ingestion: PagerDuty alert if ingestion rate < 95% over a 15m window.
- Integrity anomalies: Security notification if checksum mismatches or unexpected deletions detected.

3) Data Residency & Retention

Policy principles:
- Customer data classification determines residency and retention. Data classes: Public, Internal, Confidential, Regulated (e.g., EU/UK Health/Financial).
- Default residency: customer region (where possible) for Regulated and Confidential data.
- Export controls: prohibited without a documented exception and customer consent.

Retention table (template):
| Data class | Default retention | Archive policy | Allowed regions | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Public | 90 days | auto-delete | Global | product-data-owner |
| Internal | 1 year | 2 years cold | Global | infra-data-owner |
| Confidential | 3 years | 7 years cold | Customer-region preferred | security |
| Regulated | Customer contract | As contract / legal hold | Customer-region only | legal + security |

Implementation notes:
- Retention enforced via lifecycle policies on storage buckets with legal-hold overrides for investigations.
- Data residency enforced by routing and tagging at ingest; policy engine denies storage outside allowed regions.
- Periodic attestation: service owners must attest to correct tagging and residency quarterly.

Example lifecycle rule (AWS S3 pseudocode):
```
Rule: {
  "ID": "confidential-7yr-archive",
  "Filter": {"Tag": {"class": "confidential"}},
  "Transitions": [{"Days": 365, "StorageClass": "GLACIER"}],
  "Expiration": {"Days": 2555}
}
```

4) Secure SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle)

Goals: Embed security controls throughout design, implementation, and deployment with measurable gates.

Gates and controls:
- Design review: All new services and significant changes (>8 developer-weeks) require a Security Design Review (SDR) before architecture freeze.
- Threat modeling: Required for any system that handles Confidential or Regulated data. Use STRIDE checklist and record findings in the design doc.
- Code review: Mandatory GitHub PR reviews (2 approvers, at least one security-aware reviewer for high-risk changes).
- Static analysis: PR pipeline must pass SAST and dependency scanning; failing findings block merge except via documented exceptions.
- Secrets management: No secrets in repo; use Vault and secret-injection at runtime.
- CI/CD hardening: Build artifacts signed; pipeline runs use ephemeral runner identities; promotion requires signed attestations.

Release checklist (minimum):
1. Security checklist completed in PR template.
2. SAST and dependency scans cleared or exceptions approved.
3. SDR completed for systems handling confidential/reg data.
4. E2E smoke tests and canary observed for 24-72 hours depending on risk level.
5. Monitoring and audit hooks installed.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures

Goals: Contain, eradicate, recover, and capture evidence while preserving system and customer trust.

Severity classification and timelines:
- Sev 1 (Critical): Active data exfiltration or service compromise impacting >10% of customers — Incident response team mobilized within 15 minutes.
- Sev 2 (High): Targeted compromise or leaked credentials impacting a small set of customers — Response mobilized within 60 minutes.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Degraded non-sensitive functionality — Response within 4 hours.

Incident steps (high-level):
1. Detect & Triage: Use telemetry and alerting; declare incident and severity; notify PagerDuty and leadership.
2. Contain: Apply temporary network or auth blocks, rotate keys, revoke sessions.
3. Evidence preservation: Freeze relevant storage, snapshot VMs/containers, export audit logs to an evidence bucket (WORM).
4. Eradicate & Remediate: Patch vulnerabilities, rotate affected credentials, restore from clean artifacts.
5. Recovery: Validate functionality, remove mitigations incrementally, monitor closely.
6. Post-incident review: Root cause analysis, timeline, remediation plan, and lessons learned published within 7 business days for Sev1/2.

Evidence preservation checklist:
- Timestamped snapshot of affected hosts/containers.
- Exported audit logs with integrity manifest.
- CI/CD artifact versions and commit SHAs.
- Network flow captures (PCAP) if required.
- Communications log (who/when notified).

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Purpose: Provide a repeatable, auditable process for responding to internal audits, SOC/ISO requests, and customer compliance inquiries.

Standard workflow (90% of requests):
1. Request intake: Requests are logged in Jira project COMPLIANCE-REQS with SLA (30 business days for standard requests, 5 business days for urgent).
2. Triage: Compliance owner reviews scope and assigns evidence owners.
3. Collect: Evidence owners gather signed screenshots, configuration exports, and log extracts; use the evidence template below.
4. Package: Evidence packaged into a WORM evidence bucket under path: s3://compliance-evidence/<request-id>/<date>/ and include a manifest.txt with SHA256 checksums.
5. Review: Security reviews package and signs off.
6. Delivery: Provide evidence via secure transfer (signed URL with timebox) or upload to auditor portal.

Evidence template (plain text manifest):
- Request ID: <COMPLIANCE-1234>
- Owner: <team@redwood.ai>
- Items:
  - config/runtime-acls-2026-02-14.json (SHA256: <hash>)
  - audit-logs-authn-2026-02-13-14to15.tar.gz (SHA256: <hash>)
  - sso-roles-export-2026-02-14.csv (SHA256: <hash>)

SLA and escalation:
- If evidence cannot be produced within SLA, the owner must update the Jira with blockers within 3 business days and notify the compliance lead.

7) Risk & Exceptions

Policy: Exceptions to security controls are permitted only via documented risk exception requests that include compensating controls, a defined expiry, and an approver from security and legal for high-risk cases.

Exception workflow:
1. Submit request: Use template in JIRA EXCEPTIONS-REQ with fields: control-id, business justification, risk level, compensating controls, proposed expiry.
2. Review: Security triages and classifies risk (Low/Med/High). High-risk requires legal review.
3. Approval: Approver(s) recorded and JIRA ticket closed with an expiration date.
4. Monitoring: Approved exceptions are added to monthly exception report and reviewed quarterly.

Compensating control examples:
- Network isolation and strict ACLs when a required hardening step is delayed.
- Increased logging and shortened token TTL while a secure vault integration is completed.

Appendix: Example commands & sample artifacts

- Export SSO roles (CLI):
  - curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood/api/v1/roles > sso-roles-export-$(date +%F).csv

- Create evidence manifest (bash):
```
sha256sum * > manifest.txt
aws s3 cp manifest.txt s3://compliance-evidence/COMPLIANCE-1234/2026-03-04/ --acl bucket-owner-full-control
```
- Sample audit query (pseudo-SQL):
```
SELECT timestamp, user, action, resource FROM audit_events
WHERE action IN ('role.update','session.revoke') AND timestamp >= '2026-03-01'
```
